name: secp256k1 ECDLP decision substrate
purpose: Canonical project decisions for evaluating routes toward recovering a secp256k1 discrete logarithm. This file decides applicability, priority, evidence gates, and foundation work; data/attack_registry.json remains the detailed attack evidence encyclopedia.

canonical_ownership.experiment_authorization: repo/ECDLP_DECISION_SUBSTRATE.json bounded_experiment_authorization, with policy and hypothesis identity cross-checked against repo/RESEARCH_ENGINE_V0.json and experiments/HYPOTHESES.yaml

target_problem.output: Recover k modulo ord(P). The primary target fixes P to a generator of the prime-order secp256k1 group, so ord(P) = n.

threat_models.definition: One arbitrary public pair (P,Q) on secp256k1, no leakage, no auxiliary powers, no useful interval promise, and no attacker-chosen invalid inputs.
The group is available only through generic encoding and group-operation oracles.
The attacker receives extra structure such as many targets, reusable precomputation, an interval promise, or auxiliary powers of the secret.
Nonce bias, side channels, faults, invalid-curve acceptance, or protocol misuse leaks information beyond a plain ECDLP instance.
A sufficiently capable error-corrected quantum computer can execute an ECDLP algorithm and its reversible elliptic-curve arithmetic.

success_levels.definition: Clarifies applicability, assumptions, or a no-go boundary without improving the attack.
Improves constants or parallelization but remains Theta(sqrt(n)) for the primary target.
Provides a justified classical single-target complexity o(sqrt(n)) under the plain-input model.
Demonstrates a reproducible end-to-end recovery with a credible secp256k1 resource estimate.

required_for_route_promotion: State the exact threat model and every auxiliary input.
Prove or independently validate that the output is the requested discrete logarithm.
State asymptotic time, memory, precomputation, parallelism, and amortization separately.
Provide a reproducible artifact with pinned code, parameters, seed, environment, and output hashes.
Provide an independent validator that does not reuse the candidate algorithm's decisive logic.
Explain why observed toy scaling should persist and identify the mathematical mechanism.
Compare against the correct generic or conditioned baseline.
State what is not proved and forbid extrapolation from toy curves without a scaling argument.
subgeneric_extra_requirements: A theoretical complexity argument with explicit assumptions.
Multiple-size measurements that are consistent with the claimed exponent.
An adversarial review of hidden preprocessing, smoothness, subgroup, and data-selection assumptions.
practical_extra_requirements: End-to-end verification on the exact target or a defensible resource model for it.
A disclosure and legal review before public operational details are released.

route_status_vocabulary.guardrail: Defines a lower bound, evaluation model, or anti-overclaim boundary.
route_status_vocabulary.baseline: Best-known baseline retained for comparison; not a breakthrough route.
route_status_vocabulary.ruled_out_for_target: Its required target property is false for secp256k1 under the stated model.
route_status_vocabulary.constant_factor_only: Useful optimization with no supported asymptotic improvement.
route_status_vocabulary.open_parked: The mathematical direction is not globally disproved, but no execution is authorized.
route_status_vocabulary.conditional_only: Relevant only when extra input or amortization changes the problem.
route_status_vocabulary.separate_threat_model: Important security route that is not a plain classical ECDLP algorithm.
route_status_vocabulary.monitor: Track external progress; do not build its full formal stack now.

routes.title: Generic-group lower bound
assumptions: Generic encodings reveal no exploitable representation structure.
Complexity is measured in oracle queries with bounded success probability.
routes.known_cost: Omega(sqrt(n)) generic queries, under the exact formal model and success assumptions.
routes.current_evidence: The collision-counting core and square-root consequence are Lean-verified.
routes.success_gate: Any classical plain-input route must identify and justify the non-generic information that escapes this model.
routes.stop_condition: Reject proposals that merely relabel generic operations or hide work in preprocessing.
routes.next_action: Retain as a mandatory comparison and scope guard; no new experiment.
routes.anti_overclaim: This is not an unconditional lower bound for algorithms exploiting field representation, endomorphisms, leakage, auxiliary inputs, or quantum computation.

routes.title: Baby-step giant-step and Pollard rho
assumptions: Ord(P) is known.
No special target structure is required.
routes.known_cost: Theta(sqrt(n)) group work; BSGS uses Theta(sqrt(n)) memory while rho can use negligible memory with parallel variants.
routes.current_evidence: Core decomposition, step bound, and collision/periodicity statements are Lean-verified; implementation constants are not a secp256k1 break.
routes.success_gate: Every candidate route must beat the correct time-memory-precomputation baseline under the same input model.
routes.stop_condition: Do not present hardware scaling or parallel rho as an asymptotic improvement.
routes.next_action: Use as the benchmark comparator in the evaluation harness.
routes.anti_overclaim: A faster implementation, distributed search, or smaller constant does not change the square-root exponent.

routes.title: GLV endomorphism acceleration
assumptions: Use the secp256k1 order-3 endomorphism and its eigenvalue on the generator subgroup.
routes.known_cost: Known use is a constant-factor acceleration or search-space symmetry; no justified o(sqrt(n)) plain-input algorithm follows.
routes.current_evidence: The rational point action, eigenvalue scope on multiples of G, and orbit facts are Lean-verified.
routes.success_gate: Promotion requires a mechanism that changes relation-generation or search complexity, not only orbit size.
routes.stop_condition: Close any proposal whose only gain is a finite orbit quotient or scalar decomposition.
routes.next_action: Keep as target structure available to a selected route; do not treat it as a standalone attack.
routes.anti_overclaim: The proved GLV identities and a factor-of-three orbit reduction are structural or constant-factor facts, not a subgeneric ECDLP result.

routes.title: Pohlig-Hellman subgroup reduction
routes.applicability: the algorithm applies, but secp256k1 has no smaller prime-order factors to exploit
assumptions: A useful factorization of ord(P) into smaller factors.
routes.known_cost: Dominated by the largest prime factor of ord(P); for secp256k1 that factor is n itself.
routes.current_evidence: n is Lean-verified prime and the reduction/reconstruction algebra is formalized.
routes.success_gate: A proposal must exhibit an actual nontrivial subgroup decomposition of the target instance.
routes.stop_condition: Stop immediately for the standard generator subgroup because n is prime.
routes.next_action: Retain as a machine-checked elimination certificate.
routes.anti_overclaim: Prime order rules out this decomposition route; it does not by itself prove hardness against non-generic attacks.

routes.title: MOV, Frey-Ruck, and Tate/Weil pairing transfer
routes.applicability: no useful low-embedding-degree transfer is available for secp256k1
assumptions: The n-torsion embeds into a finite-field multiplicative group of tractable extension degree.
The relevant pairing is non-degenerate on available points.
routes.known_cost: Transfer is only useful when finite-field DLP in F_(p^k) is easier at the target's embedding degree k.
routes.current_evidence: Lean proves the secp256k1 embedding degree is greater than 100, which is a strong practical exclusion of low-degree MOV-style transfers.
routes.success_gate: A proposal must state the exact pairing, available torsion points, extension degree, and finite-field DLP cost.
routes.stop_condition: Reject low-degree-transfer claims inconsistent with the verified embedding-degree bound.
routes.next_action: Keep the target-specific exclusion; defer a full pairing library unless a new route needs it.
routes.anti_overclaim: The proved bound excludes low-degree practical transfer in the audited model; it is not a theorem that every conceivable pairing-based reduction is impossible.

routes.title: Smart, Satoh-Araki, and Semaev anomalous-curve lifting
routes.applicability: inapplicable because secp256k1 is not anomalous
assumptions: #E(F_p) = p, equivalently trace one in the relevant setting.
routes.known_cost: Polynomial-time for the anomalous special case; the prerequisite fails here.
routes.current_evidence: Lean proves the anomalous iff trace-one scope and that secp256k1 is ordinary and non-anomalous.
routes.success_gate: A p-adic proposal must identify a different valid degeneracy and prove it holds for secp256k1.
routes.next_action: Retain the formal exclusion; do not build an elliptic formal-group stack for this target now.
routes.anti_overclaim: Ruling out the anomalous-curve attack does not rule out unrelated lifting or representation-specific algorithms.

routes.title: Weil descent and GHS-style transfer
routes.applicability: the standard extension-field descent mechanism has no nontrivial degree to exploit over the prime field F_p
assumptions: The curve is defined over an extension field with exploitable descent geometry.
routes.known_cost: Useful only for selected extension-field settings; degree one gives no descent gain.
routes.current_evidence: Target-field structure rules out the standard GHS setting; no dedicated Lean theorem is claimed.
routes.success_gate: A proposal must provide a concrete alternative descent object over F_p and a lower resulting DLP cost.
routes.stop_condition: Reject arguments that silently replace the prime-field target with an extension-field family.
routes.next_action: Document as a target-applicability exclusion; no formal stack now.
routes.anti_overclaim: This excludes the standard extension-field descent setup, not every possible algebraic-geometric reformulation over a prime field.

routes.title: Prime-field index calculus
routes.applicability: conceptually direct, with no validated subgeneric secp256k1 algorithm in the audited evidence
assumptions: Efficient factor-base relation generation over a large prime field.
A tractable polynomial-system solving regime.
Linear algebra and descent costs that preserve any relation-generation gain.
routes.known_cost: No accepted plain-prime-field asymptotic improvement is established here; known toy systems encounter relation-yield, degree, and memory barriers.
routes.current_evidence: S3/S4 foundations and limited toy measurements exist, but they do not establish a degree-of-regularity law or subgeneric scaling. WCC 2017 adds bounded m=2 practicality evidence on selected small primes and explicitly makes no asymptotic claim.
routes.success_gate: Provide an exact relation system, independent EC validation, a justified solving-cost model, and multi-size evidence consistent with o(sqrt(n)).
routes.stop_condition: Park when gains rely only on factor-base constants, unvalidated Macaulay proxies, tiny fields, or hidden exhaustive enumeration.
routes.next_action: Preserve evidence and prerequisites; wait for explicit route selection before any new experiment.
routes.anti_overclaim: Solving selected toy systems or proving Semaev identities does not establish a practical or asymptotic ECDLP improvement.

routes.title: GLV-symmetrized Semaev systems
routes.applicability: direct to the j=0 target structure, but only constant-factor evidence exists
assumptions: Invariant coordinates reduce relation-generation complexity or solving degree, not only factor-base storage.
The quotient retains enough information to recover valid relations.
routes.known_cost: Finite GLV orbit compression is constant-factor. The proposed u_i=x_i^3 map is the coordinatewise C3^m quotient, not the diagonal C3 quotient, and generically merges 3^(m-1) diagonal orbits.
routes.current_evidence: GLV-SEMAEV-ITER-001 exactly enumerates all 27 S3 and 81 S4 coordinatewise C3 scalings in the universal and primitive cube-root quotients and after secp256k1 specialization. Only the diagonal C3 is a scalar polynomial covariance. Certificate 2142e8d66a8422768b609e42f5ce09377d5f93609941139fc9fc4e5abe4dfe59 gives every rejected S3/S4 pair a coefficient +1 witness over Z[b], making the polynomial classification uniform across characteristics whenever a primitive cube root exists. The fixed-target certificate is S4-specific: 9db5e0375421659f9abb905c12ae77232ef9957867f7194baaf548d45a1f091d proves that every nonzero affine S4 target has only identity coordinate-scaling covariance in characteristic outside {2,3}; the r=0 slice has exactly the diagonal C3 stabilizer. Standard-library validators independently reconstruct S4 from the Sylvester determinant and replay both classifications. Lean separately proves secp256k1_seven_not_isSquare, secp256k1_x_ne_zero, and the diagonal corollary secp256k1_glv_affine_target_moves, so no F_p-rational affine secp256k1 target inhabits r=0. Exhaustiveness is still certificate-backed, not a Lean theorem; source-author independence is not established. The original 14-theorem covariance and point-group transport module passed the full Lean build, built-source no-sorry scan, and exhaustive axiom audit in workflow run 30163027316 at content head be7a4d8e7da94b33ef74b0c146d732314b293827. The affine closeout extension requires its own build and axiom audit; earlier P0-P4 evidence is retained unchanged.
routes.success_gate: Supply a materially different exact mechanism with explicit fixed-target behavior, recovery, and a theoretical reason for a lower asymptotic solving exponent, then validate it independently. Repackaging coordinatewise cubes is not a new premise.
routes.stop_condition: The coordinatewise quotient and dependent m=3 scaling draft are stopped. Any successor also stops if its gain is bounded by orbit size or disappears after complete relation-generation and recovery costs are counted.
routes.next_action: Keep GLV-SEMAEV-ITER-001 closed without a solver run. Accept only a materially different phase-preserving mechanism with an exact recovery map, orbit tags, excluded components, a falsifiable full-cost prediction, and an independent validator through TASK-008 before any new decision.

structural_lane.scope: Exact S3/S4 scalar polynomial covariance/classification; S4-only nonzero-affine fixed-target coordinate-scaling classification plus the r=0 exception; Lean proof that the exception has no F_p-rational affine secp256k1 target; S4 target transport; and the smallest theorem package only.

routes.anti_overclaim: The diagonal-only polynomial classification closes the independent coordinatewise-cube quotient, and the S4 certificate plus the base-field affine Lean fact close its S4 fixed-target coordinate-scaling premise for F_p-rational affine secp256k1 targets. It does not cover S3 fixed-target classification, the point at infinity, extension-field targets, non-scalar or birational automorphisms, faithful Petit, Groebner/F4 complexity, or the whole GLV-Semaev route. It is not an ECDLP or secp256k1 break.

routes.title: Petit-style composed rational maps
routes.applicability: source-grounded but target applicability remains unresolved: PKC 2016 specifies a p-1-smooth construction and a separate auxiliary-curve construction whose own self-isogeny defines the root map; neither has a validated secp256k1 full-cost bridge
assumptions: A correctly specified low-degree rational map yields a useful factor-base or relation system.
Composition, solving, and recovery costs improve the full attack.
routes.known_cost: No reliable project estimate; the existing six-variable toy presentation is explicitly non-faithful and descriptive.
routes.current_evidence: The official PKC 2016 primary source has now been inspected. It defines the faithful prime-field factor base F={(x,y):L(x)=0}, with L a composition of low-degree rational maps, and gives p-1-smooth-subgroup and auxiliary-curve realizations. In the second construction the auxiliary curve only shares the base field with the target; a self-isogeny of the auxiliary curve defines the root map. The paper explicitly leaves the asymptotic complexity of the resulting generalized root-finding problem open. WCC 2017 adds bounded m=2 practicality evidence on selected small primes and a distinct p-plus-one trace extension; it cannot be transferred quantitatively to m=16 or substituted for the auxiliary curve. Historical P4 did not implement either PKC construction and remains only an inconclusive negative control; it is not evidence against the faithful route. For nonsingular y^2=x^3+7 in characteristic not in {2,3,7}, TASK-017 independently replayed an exact set-theoretic homogeneous projective S3-tree bridge, every named exceptional lift and identity stratum, deterministic supplied-coordinate recovery, and raw and compressed secp256k1 GLV lift-sign checks. TASK-018 freezes the recursive projective S17 contract, including fixed degrees and the literal Sylvester determinant under the frozen coefficient, argument, and row order. TASK-019 kernel-checks the fixed-degree projective resultant common-root theorem, coefficient-map and algebraic-closure reflection variants, the literal TASK-018 Sylvester matrix and determinant with coefficient unit 1, and its end-to-end common-root corollary. Formal-degree drops, zero forms, affine witnesses, and [1:0] are retained without primitive/content, monic, or actual-degree normalization. The TASK-019 non-run binding is PKC-SMOOTH-M16-PROJECTIVE-RESULTANT-KERNEL-001 with SHA-256 0b9d8b48953aae2defa28ade67992084cecca3a01b43490bc338a0fd5ce97c5a and typed claim SC-PKC-M16-PROJECTIVE-RESULTANT-KERNEL-RESULT. TASK-020 kernel-checks the actual recursive frozen C_r family, exact same-field and coefficient-map successor specialization at formal degrees (2^(r-2),2), coefficient unit 1, affine [y:1] and infinity [1:0] output branches, the uniform predecessor output-degree bound, and the unconditional one-step resultant/common-projective-root equivalence. routes.stop_condition: Reject low-bit filters, redundant auxiliary variables, or presentation-only degree changes as substitutes for the cited construction.
routes.next_action: Keep the route parked. TASK-023 through TASK-025 completed the exact chart cover, necessary infinity-stratum filters, and conditional single-affine-chart propagation. TASK-026 then consumed its one external synthetic-toy authorization: all 3000000 trials completed, 911 exact relations were accepted, 907 were affine regular, and all six curve-arm regularity gates passed. REO-2026-07-31-001 records the result. This supports the bounded enabling claim that the named regular locus is usable in the frozen toy construction. Matched orbit/plain controls retained no H_NEW qualifying size, so the GLV-specific explanation is bounded negative and the terminal is CLASSIFY_AS_KNOWN_LOCAL_SIMPLIFICATION. The result is not source-faithful PKC relation generation, rank, solver scaling, recovery, total cost, 256-bit persistence, or an ECDLP improvement. Only formulate and review a source-faithful, non-executable HYP-M16-SOLVER-SLOPE-001 proposal with end-to-end metrics and scaling death criteria. Keep every TASK-026 rerun, production mask sweep, solver, experiment, route rejection, route promotion, cost claim, and exact-target inference closed until a separate dated authorization. Keep the auxiliary-curve cell parked until a primary source supplies a finite family or search domain with a completeness criterion.
routes.anti_overclaim: The existing P4 experiment is not a faithful Petit implementation and cannot support a claim about the original method.

routes.title: Elliptic divisibility sequences and division-polynomial re-encodings
routes.applicability: structurally direct, with no known independent information source or subgeneric inversion method
assumptions: A sequence or polynomial observable can be inverted more cheaply than scalar multiplication or exhaustive apparition search.
routes.known_cost: Known recurrences evaluate W_m for a supplied m; they do not cheaply find the unknown first zero or discrete logarithm.
routes.current_evidence: Lean formalizes substantial division-polynomial and normEDS structure. Toy measurements confirm apparition/torsion equivalence and no advantage.
routes.success_gate: Identify an observable computable from (P,Q) whose inversion provably avoids equivalent ECDLP work.
routes.stop_condition: Stop when the construction only re-encodes scalar multiplication or requires Theta(ord(P)) search.
routes.next_action: Keep HYP_WARD_EDS_001 parked; finish no additional point-division bridge unless a selected route needs it.
routes.anti_overclaim: A fast recurrence for a known index and a verified torsion identity do not solve for an unknown scalar.

routes.title: Isogeny, endomorphism-ring, and Frobenius transfer
routes.applicability: no concrete efficiently computable transfer to a weaker target is identified
assumptions: An efficiently computable map reaches a curve or representation where DLP is materially easier.
Kernel and degree do not erase the gain.
routes.known_cost: Unspecified without a concrete target and map; special endomorphisms currently support constant-factor GLV acceleration.
routes.current_evidence: The repository has target endomorphism facts but no general isogeny stack or candidate weak codomain.
routes.success_gate: Provide an explicit map, target, DLP advantage, and end-to-end cost.
routes.stop_condition: Do not formalize a general stack in advance of a concrete route.
routes.next_action: Monitor literature and reuse GLV facts; no build now.
routes.anti_overclaim: Complex multiplication and a nontrivial endomorphism do not imply a transfer to an easier DLP.

routes.title: Multi-target and reusable-precomputation tradeoffs
routes.applicability: not applicable to the primary one-target/no-precomputation objective unless costs are explicitly amortized
assumptions: Many targets share a group or base point.
Precomputation storage and setup are available and counted separately.
routes.known_cost: Can change amortized constants and time-memory tradeoffs; it does not by itself solve an arbitrary single target below the proper total-cost baseline.
routes.current_evidence: Covered in the attack registry as a separate conditioned model.
routes.success_gate: State target count, online/offline split, memory, reuse horizon, and total amortized cost.
routes.stop_condition: Reject comparisons that omit precomputation or compare an amortized online phase to a full single-target baseline.
routes.next_action: Represent in the evaluation contract; no experiment in this phase.
routes.anti_overclaim: An improved online phase after large reusable work is not a plain single-target break.

routes.title: Interval DLP, partial-key knowledge, and auxiliary-power algorithms
routes.applicability: not applicable to an arbitrary full-range scalar without the promised interval or auxiliary data
assumptions: k lies in a known small interval, or the attacker receives additional algebraic powers or relations involving k.
routes.known_cost: May reduce work relative to the conditioned search space; it does not alter the unconditioned n-sized instance.
routes.current_evidence: The current target contract supplies neither an interval promise nor auxiliary powers.
routes.success_gate: Declare exactly how the auxiliary information is obtained and include its acquisition cost.
routes.stop_condition: Reject any route that assumes the secret information it is meant to recover.
routes.next_action: Keep as a scope category for future protocol or leakage analyses.
routes.anti_overclaim: Conditioned algorithms solve a different input problem unless the extra information is independently available.

routes.title: Hidden-number and lattice attacks on biased or reused ECDSA nonces
routes.applicability: important for key security but not a plain ECDLP algorithm
assumptions: Signatures leak nonce bits, reuse nonces, or have a statistically exploitable bias.
routes.known_cost: Depends on leakage quality, sample count, and lattice dimension; a valid instance can recover a signing key without solving arbitrary ECDLP.
routes.current_evidence: The repository catalogs the attack family but lacks an LLL/BKZ and HNP formal stack.
routes.success_gate: Keep leakage acquisition, statistical model, lattice reduction, and key verification explicit.
routes.stop_condition: Do not classify nonce failures as a mathematical break of secp256k1 ECDLP.
routes.next_action: Preserve as a separate security track; no lattice foundation build for the primary objective now.
routes.anti_overclaim: Recovering keys from bad nonces demonstrates an implementation or protocol failure, not a generic ECDLP solver.

routes.title: Invalid-curve, twist, fault, and side-channel routes
routes.applicability: relevant only when an implementation exposes attacker-controlled inputs or physical leakage
assumptions: Missing point validation, unsafe scalar multiplication, fault injection, timing, power, cache, or electromagnetic leakage.
routes.known_cost: Implementation-dependent and often far below generic DLP when the vulnerability exists.
routes.current_evidence: Protocol algebra is formalized at an abstract level; implementation leakage is outside that proof model.
routes.success_gate: Specify the concrete implementation, leakage channel, validation behavior, and key-recovery verification.
routes.stop_condition: Keep mathematical protocol soundness separate from implementation hardening claims.
routes.next_action: Record scope; do not expand the Lean substrate until a concrete implementation-verification goal exists.
routes.anti_overclaim: A vulnerable implementation can expose a key even though the underlying plain ECDLP remains unchanged.

routes.title: Fault-tolerant quantum ECDLP
routes.applicability: algorithmically direct given sufficiently capable fault-tolerant quantum hardware
assumptions: Large-scale error-corrected quantum computation.
A reversible elliptic-curve implementation with the quoted logical resources.
Physical error correction overhead is separately accounted for.
routes.known_cost: Polynomial-time quantum algorithm. The 2026 audited preprint reports 835 logical qubits and 2^30.63 Toffoli gates for secp256k1; physical resources and availability are not established by that estimate.
routes.current_evidence: Shor gives the algorithmic route; Luo et al. provide the current project-tracked logical-resource estimate.
routes.success_gate: Distinguish algorithm, logical circuit, error-correction overhead, physical hardware, runtime, and availability.
routes.stop_condition: Do not turn a logical-resource estimate into a claim that present hardware can break secp256k1.
routes.next_action: Update the registry estimate and monitor primary literature; do not build a quantum Lean stack now.
routes.anti_overclaim: This is a separate computational threat model and a future resource risk, not a classical secp256k1 break or evidence of current operational capability.

foundations.title: Scalar-parity and bit-security reduction and Fourier layer
foundations.mathlib_status: Every file of the PR #444 port imports Mathlib, directly or through a sibling statement file. The layer uses Mathlib's ZMod arithmetic, finite sums, additive characters, complex exponentials, Real.cos, Real.sin, Real.sqrt, Real.pi, and real logarithms, and states the halving reduction for any additive commutative group through addOrderOf. The port extended by FD-2026-10-22-002 also uses Mathlib's Weierstrass affine point group and its slope (the zeta statements and the x-coordinate instances) and Mathlib's Hoeffding bound for bounded random variables under a finite uniform product measure (the majority-vote step of the noisy reduction). A lexical search of the pinned Mathlib tag v4.31.0 on 2026-10-22 found no discrete-logarithm, hard-core-bit, or bit-security module.
foundations.deliverable: Only the bounded layer authorized by FD-2026-10-22-001 and extended by FD-2026-10-22-002: the PR #444 port of theorems already kernel-checked in the owner's companion lab repository. They are a halving reduction that recovers a discrete logarithm from an exact parity oracle correct on every multiple of the generator, the Fourier spectrum of the parity sign, ordered-sector and carry-sign facts for a cube root of unity modulo a prime, Fourier concentration and balance bounds for the ordered-sector sign, and a transfer inequality that takes a twisted character-sum bound as an assumed hypothesis. Under FD-2026-10-22-002 it also takes exactly one further port, after PR #444, of 34 theorems already kernel-checked in that lab repository: exact zero-correlation identities for even and odd features, a Fourier transfer bound and L1 bounds of the ordered-sector and carry signs, the slope cocycle and the Weierstrass zeta function of a short-normal-form curve, a heavy-coefficient lemma and the correctness of the hard-core reduction for the ordered-sector sign with the sparse Fourier transform output as a hypothesis, relabelling with a defect and the exact-branch reduction, the window law, and a halving reduction from a deterministic noisy parity predictor with its failure bound. Transfer bounds keep their character-sum bounds as assumed hypotheses. The layer is not a hardness theorem, constructs no parity oracle, formalizes no cost, and states nothing specific to secp256k1.
foundations.resume_condition: Any build in this area beyond FD-2026-10-22-002, such as the sparse Fourier transform step or a cost model for the reductions, a proof of a twisted-sum bound for an elliptic-curve coordinate map, or a parity-correlation experiment, requires a new dated decision.

foundations.title: Exact rational-point counts for prime-order short Weierstrass curves
foundations.mathlib_status: Mathlib provides the Weierstrass point group; in the pinned tag v4.31.0 the number of points appears only as an input to the L-function definition. A lexical search on 2026-10-22 found no Hasse bound and no Schoof-type point-counting theorem.
foundations.deliverable: Only the bounded build authorized by FD-2026-10-22-001: the PR #446 curve-generic count #E(F) = n for an elliptic short Weierstrass curve over a finite field F that has a point of order n, satisfies 2*#F + 1 < 3n, and has no 2-torsion, proved from the elementary bound #E(F) <= 2*#F + 1 rather than the Hasse bound; kernel-checked no-2-torsion certificates for nine named prime-order curves; and #E = n for the repository's P-256. The secp256k1 exact count already exists separately. Counts for cofactor > 1 curves, a Hasse bound, and unconditional counts for the other seven named curves are outside this deliverable.
foundations.resume_condition: A new dated decision is required for further point-counting work (a Hasse bound, Schoof-type counting, cofactor > 1 curves, or unconditional counts for further curves) and for adding p256-exact-cardinality to release.required_nodes.

foundation_build_decisions.source: Owner instruction of 2026-10-22 on draft PRs #444, #446, and #447, recorded in the owner's companion lab repository as ADR 0024.
foundation_build_decisions.rationale: AUTONOMY.md requires a dated change to this file before a new formal-foundation build, and its unlock rule describes that change as selecting a route. None of these builds is attack work, so the owner authorizes them without selecting any route. The vocabulary has no decision value for an authorized build without a selected route: build_now means directly needed to evaluate every candidate or to keep project state coherent, and the checker requires it to be P0 and complete; build_if_selected waits for a selected route; monitor_only forbids construction. Both new foundations are therefore retain_frontier with build_now false, and this record bounds the authorized build to exactly the named pull request, with an exact uncertainty, a success condition, and a stop condition. It neither selects nor promotes a route and does not supersede RS-2026-07-24-001.

rulings.authorized_build: Exactly the port in PR #444 of twenty theorems already kernel-checked in the owner's companion lab repository, with their ledger rows and generated views: the exact-oracle halving reduction, the parity Fourier spectrum, the ordered-sector and carry-sign facts, the Fourier concentration and balance bounds of the ordered-sector sign, and the transfer inequality under an assumed twisted-sum bound.
rulings.exact_uncertainty: Whether any efficiently computable public function of a point correlates with the parity of its discrete logarithm at or above the break-even bias, the predictor advantage at which a parity-oracle reduction would match the generic square-root cost. The authorized layer proves a reduction from an exact oracle and Fourier tools only; it decides no correlation and proves no hardness.
rulings.success_condition: CI kernel-checks every ported theorem, and the full-ledger axiom audit shows that each depends only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound, with no native_decide and no custom axiom. The ledger rows state the exact-oracle and assumed twisted-sum hypotheses and make no hardness or secp256k1 claim.
rulings.stop_condition: The authorization covers PR #444 only and ends when it is merged or closed. Any further build in this area requires a new dated decision.
rulings.status_basis: The implementation lands with PR #444. implementation_status partial records the state after that merge, which follows this decision's pull request (#449) in the same merge sequence, with only PR #446, which does not touch this foundation, merged between them. Until PR #444 merges, the theorems exist only in the owner's companion lab repository. If PR #444 closes unmerged, a new dated decision resets this foundation's implementation_status.

rulings.authorized_build: Exactly the formal build in PR #446: the curve-generic exact count from a point of order n, the elementary bound #E(F) <= 2*#F + 1, and a no-2-torsion certificate; the certificates for nine named prime-order curves, whose soundness lemma is adapted from pyca/verified-garbage, which already kernel-checks no-2-torsion for the same nine curves and #E = n for P-256, P-384, and P-521 on its own curve type, with that prior work disclosed; and #E = n for the repository's P-256.
rulings.exact_uncertainty: Whether the exact group order of a prime-order short Weierstrass curve, in particular the repository's P-256, can be kernel-checked from a point of order n and a no-2-torsion certificate without formalizing the Hasse bound or Schoof's algorithm. It carries no attack information.
rulings.success_condition: CI kernel-checks the curve-generic count, the certificates, and #E = n for P-256, and the trust base of each new declaration, kernel-only or inherited compiler trust, is disclosed per declaration.
rulings.stop_condition: The authorization covers PR #446 only and ends when it is merged or closed. p256-exact-cardinality is not added to release.required_nodes. Further point-counting work or a release-node change requires a new dated decision.

rulings.authorized_build: Exactly one pull request, after PR #444, that ports the 34 theorems in lab_declarations, already kernel-checked in the owner's companion lab repository, with their statements unchanged, their statement definitions, the supporting definitions and lemmas of their proof files, their ledger rows and generated views. The names are relative to the lab namespace KeyaiFormal, which PR #444 maps to Ecdlp.ParityFourier with unchanged short names. By block: K, exact zero correlation over the nonzero scalars of even features with the parity and carry signs (and, for n = 3 mod 4, the Legendre symbol) and of odd features with the ordered-sector sign (and, for n = 1 mod 4, the Legendre symbol), including any function of the x-coordinate on any Weierstrass curve; CT, a Fourier transfer bound for any complex functions under an assumed twisted-sum bound, L1 bounds of the ordered-sector and carry signs, and lowest-bit transfer bounds against both signs under an assumed twisted-sum bound; Zeta, the slope 2-cocycle of a short-normal-form curve over a field, the Weierstrass zeta function as its coboundary when the point count is a unit, additivity of the slope sum when it is zero, and lowest-bit transfer bounds for the zeta function conditional on an assumed twisted-sum bound for it; C44H and C44R, a heavy-coefficient lemma, the correlation and table-count lemmas, a Parseval bound on the number of heavy frequencies, and the correctness of the hard-core reduction for the ordered-sector sign with the sparse Fourier transform output taken as a hypothesis; C37, relabelling a predictor by a public sign with a defect, recovery of the discrete logarithm from an exact branch oracle and a public label, and the sign relation between two square roots of the same nonzero element; W, the window law; PB, a majority-vote bound, the vote identity and vote advantage, and a halving reduction from a deterministic parity predictor with arbitrarily placed errors and a uniform random shift table, with its failure bound, in ZMod n and in any group with an element of odd prime order.
rulings.exact_uncertainty: Unchanged from FD-2026-10-22-001: whether any efficiently computable public function of a point correlates with the parity of its discrete logarithm at or above the break-even bias. The extension proves exact zero-correlation identities for symmetric features, transfer bounds under assumed character-sum bounds, the correctness of reductions whose algorithmic inputs (the sparse Fourier transform output, an exact branch oracle, a noisy predictor) are hypotheses, and a failure bound for the noisy reduction; it decides no correlation, formalizes no cost, and proves no hardness.
rulings.success_condition: CI kernel-checks every ported theorem with its statement unchanged from the lab's frozen statement, and the full-ledger axiom audit shows that each depends only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound, with no native_decide and no custom axiom. The ledger rows state the assumed hypotheses (the twisted-sum bounds, including the one for the zeta function, the sparse Fourier transform output, the exact branch oracle, the square-root relation, and the deterministic predictor with its error fraction) and make no hardness, cost, or secp256k1 claim.
rulings.stop_condition: The authorization covers that one pull request only and ends when it is merged or closed; because the port builds on the PR #444 files, PR #444 merges first. Any further build in this area, such as the sparse Fourier transform step, a cost model or break-even bound, the hard-core lemma or reduction for the carry sign, a proof of a twisted-sum bound for an elliptic-curve coordinate map or for the zeta function, or a parity-correlation experiment, requires a new dated decision.
